passage_text: Researchers studied the impact of light intensity on the growth of the model plant *Arabidopsis thaliana*. Plants at the onset of bolting were divided into four experimental groups exposed to different light intensities (photosynthetic photon flux densities of 200, 400, 800, and 1600 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹) for 21 days. Measurements taken at the end of the period included average shoot (flowering-stem) height (cm), average root length (cm), and chlorophyll concentration (mg g⁻¹). The results, summarized in Table 1, show a positive correlation between light intensity and shoot height up to 800 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, after which the growth plateaued. Root length increased steadily with light intensity, while chlorophyll concentration peaked at 800 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ and declined slightly at 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, suggesting photoinhibition at the highest intensity. These findings suggest that moderate light levels optimize shoot growth and chlorophyll content in *A. thaliana*.
stem: Which of the following best describes the relationship between light intensity and shoot height in *Arabidopsis thaliana* as reported in the study?

options.A: Shoot height increases linearly with light intensity across all levels.
options.B: Shoot height peaks at 800 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ and then declines at 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.
options.C: Shoot height increases with light intensity up to 800 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ and then plateaus.
options.D: Shoot height is unaffected by light intensity.

explanation: Correct: C) Shoot height rose from 12.4 cm (200) to 18.9 cm (400) and 26.3 cm (800), then only to 27.0 cm at 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹: an increase up to 800 followed by a plateau. Why the others are wrong: A) the gains are not constant (the rise per 100 µmol drops to almost nothing above 800), so the relationship is not linear. B) shoot height did not decline at 1600; it rose slightly from 26.3 to 27.0 cm. D) shoot height clearly depended on light, rising from 12.4 to 27.0 cm.
trap: Reading the chlorophyll decline at 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ as a decline in shoot height, when shoot height actually rose slightly (26.3 to 27.0 cm).

stem: Which additional group would best show whether shoot height rises, stays level or falls at light intensities above those tested, while changing only one variable?

options.A: A group exposed to 2000 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ (about full sunlight) for 21 days
options.B: A group exposed to 800 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ for 42 days
options.C: A group exposed to 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ with a 12-hour dark period each day
options.D: A group exposed to 200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ for 21 days

explanation: Correct: A) a 2000 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ group extends the intensity series beyond 1600 under the same 21-day conditions, changing only light intensity. Why the others are wrong: B) Changes duration as well as intensity and does not extend the intensity range. C) Changes the photoperiod, introducing a second variable. D) Repeats an intensity already tested and gives no information above 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.
trap: Choosing a design that varies time or photoperiod instead of extending intensity alone.

stem: What is the percent increase in average shoot height from 200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ to 800 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹?
explanation: Correct: A) (26.3 − 12.4)/12.4 × 100 = 112%. Why the others are wrong: B) 68% does not follow from 12.4 and 26.3. C) 53% divides the 13.9 cm gain by the final height (26.3) instead of the starting height. D) 88% does not follow from 12.4 and 26.3.
trap: Dividing the change by the final value (13.9 / 26.3 = 53%) uses the wrong denominator.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by Table 1?

options.A: Shoot height at 800 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ was more than double the shoot height at 200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.
options.B: Root length increased at every higher light intensity.
options.C: Chlorophyll concentration was lower at 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ than at 800 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.
options.D: Shoot height at 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ was substantially greater than at 800 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.

explanation: Correct: shoot height rose only from 26.3 to 27.0 cm between 800 and 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ (0.7 cm), a plateau. Why the others are wrong: A) 26.3 / 12.4 = 2.1, so this is supported. B) Root length rose 5.8, 7.6, 9.3, 10.1 cm, so this is supported. C) 4.7 is lower than 5.0 mg/g, so this is supported.
trap: Assuming growth keeps increasing because the intensity doubled.

stem: The authors attribute the slight chlorophyll decline at 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ to photoinhibition. Which of the following best links that interpretation to a broader ecological principle?

options.A: Plants adapted to high light dissipate excess excitation energy by non-photochemical quenching (xanthophyll cycle) and often have thicker, smaller leaves.
options.B: Light intensity is the sole determinant of plant growth in all ecosystems.
options.C: Root development is independent of shoot growth.
options.D: Chlorophyll concentration always increases with light intensity.

explanation: Correct: A) Excess excitation energy at high light damages photosystem II; sun-adapted plants limit this with non-photochemical quenching (the xanthophyll cycle) and often have thicker, smaller leaves. Why the others are wrong: B) light is not the sole determinant of growth; water, nutrients and CO₂ also matter. C) root and shoot growth are coordinated, and the table shows root length increasing along with shoot height. D) chlorophyll did not always increase with light; it fell from 5.0 to 4.7 mg g⁻¹ at 1600 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.
trap: Picking an absolute claim such as light being the sole determinant of growth, which one Arabidopsis experiment cannot show and which ignores water, nutrients and CO2.
